record_type_quote:
The purposes of the current study were to
systematically replicate and extend Griffen et al.
(1998). The study replicated Griffen et al. by
evaluating (a) a continuous presentation schedule of secondary targets during which a secondary target was presented following every
primary target in a session and (b) an intermittent schedule of secondary targets during which
a secondary target was presented every four trials during a session.

targets.authors: Griffen, A. K., Schuster, J. W., & Morse, T. E.
targets.title: The acquisition of instructive feedback: A comparison of continuous versus intermittent presentation schedules.
targets.evidence_quote:
The purposes of the current study were to
systematically replicate and extend Griffen et al.
(1998). The study replicated Griffen et al. by
evaluating (a) a continuous presentation schedule of secondary targets during which a secondary target was presented following every
primary target in a session and (b) an intermittent schedule of secondary targets during which
a secondary target was presented every four trials during a session.
targets.outcome_quote:
Similar to the ﬁndings of Griffen
et al. (1998), the current study found that
intermittent presentation of secondary targets
during IF was more efﬁcient than a continuous
presentation schedule of secondary targets.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly compare the central finding with Griffen and report the same advantage of intermittent presentation. Variations between the two new intermittent schedules do not contradict the target finding.

reasoning: New participants re-test the published schedule comparison by Griffen et al. Other IF studies supply background and procedural context rather than independently re-tested findings.
